paragraphs.text: Four seconds separated Channing Lane’s first steal from the basket she helped create Saturday in Macon, Georgia. The sophomore guard from Pontotoc took the ball away with 8:27 left in the first quarter and set up Lena Taylor for a layup. That put Blue Mountain ahead 8–1 on the way to a 91–52 win over Wesleyan.

Three of her steals were followed by layups. The exception came midway through the second quarter, when Isabella Aversa made a three-pointer three seconds after Lane took the ball away. Early in the third quarter, Lane finished the play herself. She came up with a steal at 8:49 and made a layup two seconds later for a 55–31 lead. Later that quarter, she stole the ball at 4:11 and fed Dominique Collins for a layup at 4:09. Blue Mountain had scored nine points within four seconds of Lane’s four steals. She finished with four assists and four rebounds in 24 minutes.

It was the second straight win in which Lane set up four baskets. In a 78–66 home win over Central Baptist on Nov. 17, she also scored 10 points. Across the two wins she made all six of her free throws, four against Central Baptist and two at Wesleyan.

Blue Mountain takes a 7–1 record into its next game, at home against Point University on Thursday, Dec. 3. Tipoff is set for 5:30 p.m. The Wesleyan win evened Blue Mountain’s conference record at 1–1.
